input: ribbons is an ordinary list/array of n <= 10000000 integers in [0,1000000000]; k is an integer in [1,1000000000]. Empty input is allowed. Python integers exclude bool; standard containers/built-ins only. Preconditions are declared, not checked. Size bounds do not promise runtime feasibility.
return: Return the largest positive integer length allowing at least k pieces cut from the ribbons; return zero if impossible.
mutation_aliasing: No caller-owned input is mutated. No state survives on the Solution instance. Scalar/string results have value semantics; private work containers do not escape.
numeric: No bitwise narrowing. Midpoint is between low+1 and high, so division never uses zero. Because iteration stops at pieces >= k, the largest temporary count is less than k+1000000000, a safe integer.
complexity: O(n * (1 + log(maximum ribbon + 1))) time and O(1) auxiliary space. Feasibility uses a capped early-exit count and upper-midpoint binary search.
